processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Held for 180 s to homogenize the austenite phase.
Cooled to the deformation temperature (1150 °C) at 10 °C/s.
Kept for 60 s to reduce the temperature fluctuations.

Constant-temperature compression to true strain 0.9; effective strain rate range 0.01–10 s^-1 (specific strain rate for the 1150 °C sample is not separately listed in the figure captions; the experimental programme reports 0.01–10 s^-1).
Quenched in water immediately after constant deformation to freeze the high-temperature microstructure morphology.

structures.overall_structure: As-quenched martensitic microstructure (prior austenite grains frozen by water quenching after hot compression at 1150 °C); the prior austenite grains are reconstructed from EBSD data.
structures.microstructure_counts: DRX fraction vs time at 1150 °C (Fig. 6(d)): all four strain-rate curves (0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 s^-1) reach DRX fraction 1.0; sigmoid transitions occur near 0.01–0.05 s (10 s^-1), 0.1–0.5 s (1 s^-1), 2–3 s (0.1 s^-1) and 20–40 s (0.01 s^-1); experimental and simulated curves are nearly coincident.

microstructure_list.region: center of the side section (specimens split along the axial direction)

measurement_conditions.environment: hot compression in Gleeble 1500 thermomechanical simulator; tantalum foil between specimen ends and indenter
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: compressed to true strain 0.9; water quenched after deformation

stress_strain_curves: 1150 °C_0.01 s⁻¹ (green): peaks between the 40 and 60 MPa gridlines then softens.
1150 °C_0.1 s⁻¹ (magenta): peaks near the 60–70 MPa level and declines.
1150 °C_1 s⁻¹ (blue): peaks near the 80–90 MPa band.
1150 °C_10 s⁻¹ (red): rises to just above the 110 MPa gridline.
Panel y-axis range 20–120 MPa; x-axis true strain 0–0.8; simulated dashed curves closely follow experimental curves.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: sections ground with SiC papers, polished with 1 μm and 0.25 μm diamond pastes, etched with saturated picric acid abluent solution
characterization_methods.purpose: observe prior austenite grain (PAG) microstructure at the center of the side section
characterization_methods.key_findings: Prior austenite grains were imaged; Image Pro Plus used to calculate equivalent diameter of each PAG.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SU5000 scanning electron microscope equipped with an EBSD detector
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: electrolytic polishing with 10% perchlorate alcohol solution at 30 V and 0.25 A for 30 s; EBSD step size 0.65–1.3 μm
characterization_methods.purpose: characterize as-quenched martensitic microstructure and reconstruct prior austenite grains
characterization_methods.key_findings: EBSD maps used to reconstruct prior austenite grains (PAGs) and distinguish recrystallized grains from deformed ones using GOS threshold of 3°.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ARPGE software (Greninger-Troiano orientation relationship); AZtecCrystal software (GOS threshold 3°); Image Pro Plus
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: boundaries with misorientation angles higher than 10° considered for PAG equivalent diameter
characterization_methods.purpose: reconstruct prior austenite grains from EBSD data and quantify DRX fraction
characterization_methods.key_findings: Recrystallized grains distinguished from deformed grains by GOS values with threshold 3°.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: DEFORM 3D software (constitutive model embedded via Fortran)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: simulation of high-temperature deformation during hot compression
characterization_methods.purpose: validate the constitutive model against experimental results under constant and varying deformation conditions
characterization_methods.key_findings: Simulation accuracy verified by comparison with experimental results.

computational_details.simulation_method: phenomenological constitutive model (modified Model 2: STG-based flow stress, modified t0.5 and stress softening coefficient ks)
computational_details.software_used: DEFORM 3D (constitutive model embedded using Fortran language)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: hot compression; constant deformation conditions 850–1150 °C and effective strain rates 0.01–10 s^-1
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Constant conditions (Table 2): Flow stress RMSE = 4.8944 MPa, R² = 0.9909, AARE = 3.91 %; Load RMSE = 274.6820 N, R² = 0.9918, AARE = 6.65 %.

analytical_models.model_name: Sellars-Tegart-Garofalo (STG) phenomenological constitutive model with modified t0.5 and stress softening coefficient
analytical_models.equation_role: characteristic stresses (yield, steady-state, saturation, critical) and DRX fraction evolution
analytical_models.model_note: Material parameters obtained by genetic algorithm (GA) optimization; constants used in the constitutive model.

computational_details.simulation_method: 3D cellular automaton (CA) with inhomogeneous dislocation density and grain boundary sliding (GBS)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: RVE 550 μm × 550 μm × 550 μm; cell size L0 = 2.5 μm; initial dislocation density 1 × 10^11 m^-2; initial mixed-grain microstructure (2D metallograph AGS 141.66 μm, SD 54.54 μm, Min 10.22 μm, Max 265.20 μm).
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The modified 3D CA reproduced experimental flow stress and microstructure (DRX fraction, AGS) under constant conditions; the 1150 °C flow-stress and DRX-fraction curves closely matched experiments (Fig. 6(d), Fig. 7(d)).

analytical_models.equation_role: GBS strain rate, nucleation, grain growth, dislocation-density evolution
analytical_models.model_note: CA model parameters from previous research or GA optimization (Appendix B1).

unmapped_findings: For the 1150 °C constant-deformation sample, no specific average prior-austenite grain size (AGS) value is reported in the text; quantitative AGS/microstructure data in the paper are given for 850 °C, 950 °C and 1050 °C conditions (Figs. 12, 19–21 and Tables 6–7).

At 1150 °C the DRX-fraction curves (Fig. 6(d)) all reach 1.0 and shift to shorter times compared with 850–1050 °C, indicating the highest-temperature, fastest complete recrystallization among the constant-deformation temperatures studied.
